dedupe_keys.name: king county washington green stormwater infrastructure retrofit monitoring echo lake and federal way

description: This case study is King County's account of two stormwater retrofit monitoring projects funded in 2015 by the state Stormwater Action Monitoring Program to find out how well green stormwater infrastructure removes pollutants. At Echo Lake in Shoreline, bioretention planter boxes draining highway, commercial and residential land reduced most measured pollutants by 81 to 99 percent even after three to five years, but nutrients were not reduced and sometimes rose, which matters for toxic algae, and inlets clogged with debris without regular clearing. At the South 356th Street regional detention facility in Federal Way, two bioretention facilities treating a 23-acre commercial basin and a wetland pond complex were metered and sampled at inlets and outlets; all treatments reduced and delayed peak flows, and the system cut suspended solids, organic contaminants and metals but increased nutrients and dissolved lead. Coverage: two sites, before and after treatment, with fact sheets, final reports and quality assurance plans as project documents. Access: free web page and reports; licence not stated. Caveats: two sites and limited years, and the page summarises, not tabulating results. It supplies measured performance to calibrate and check retrofit design models for stormwater treatment and peak-flow simulation, and lists no linked catalogue records.
